skills.name: Use similarity: maps, models, areas and volumes

note.text:
Scale drawings, maps and models are similar to the real objects.
• A map scale 1 : n means 1 cm on the map is n cm on the ground. Lengths × n; areas × n².
• Convert units carefully: 100 000 cm = 1 km, so 1 cm² on a 1 : 100 000 map is 1 km².
• Models: a model car on a scale 1 : 20 is 20 times shorter, 400 times smaller in area, 8000 times smaller in volume.
• Costs that depend on area (paint) scale by k²; those that depend on volume (contents, mass) by k³.

sections.heading: Maps and scale
sections.text:
A map is a similar copy of the land, shrunk by its scale. A scale of {1} : {50000} means {1} cm on the map stands for {50000} cm on the ground, which is {500} m.
Lengths: multiply by {50000}. Areas: multiply by {50000}² because area uses two lengths.
Change units at the end: {100} cm = {1} m, {100000} cm = {1} km, {10000} m² = {1} hectare.

sections.heading: Models
sections.text:
A model built on a scale of {1} : {20} has every length {20} times smaller than the real thing.
• Its surface area is {20}² = {400} times smaller.
• Its volume is {20}³ = {8000} times smaller.
A model car may look the same, but it would hold only a tiny amount of fuel.

sections.heading: Paying for area or volume
sections.text:
Ask what the quantity depends on.
• Paint, cloth, tiles: area, so factor k².
• Contents, mass, amount of oil or water: volume, so factor k³.
A tin twice as tall (and similar) holds {8} times as much oil, so it should cost about {8} times as much, not twice.

key_words.meaning: {1} : n, one map unit for n real units

mistake.wrong: Map {1} : {1000}: {4} cm² on the map is {4000} cm² on the ground
mistake.why: Areas scale by the square of the map scale.

worked_example.problem: A map of a farm near Kumba has scale {1} : {n}. A field has area {A} cm² on the map. Find its real area in hectares ({1} ha = {10000} m²).
steps: {1} cm on the map = {n} cm = {n / 100} m on the ground.

cards.idea: On a map {1} : n, lengths are multiplied by n and areas by n².
Convert units at the end: {1} km = {100000} cm.
Paint depends on area (k²); contents and mass depend on volume (k³).
example: A tank twice as wide, long and high needs {4} times the paint and holds {8} times the water.

check.prompt: A tin of paint covers a small model water tank. A similar real tank is {k} times as long. How many tins are needed for the real tank?

misconceptions.explain: Paint depends on area: use k², not k.
k³ would be for the water it holds; paint covers area.

solution: Paint covers area: area factor = {k}² = {k * k}.

questions.prompt: A map has scale {1} : {n}. A road is {d} cm long on the map. How long is it in real life, in metres?

misconceptions.explain: That is in centimetres. Divide by {100} for metres.
Multiply by the scale number: the real road is longer.

questions.prompt: On a map of scale {1} : {100000}, a lake covers {A} cm². What is its real area in km²?

misconceptions.explain: Convert: {100000} cm is {1} km, so each cm² is {1} km².

solution: {1} cm on the map = {100000} cm = {1} km.
So {1} cm² on the map = {1} km², and {A} cm² = {answer} km².

questions.prompt: A model of a minibus is made on a scale of {1} : {k}. The real minibus has a floor area of {F} m². What is the floor area of the model, in cm²?

misconceptions.explain: Areas scale by k², not k.
Convert m² to cm²: {1} m² = {10000} cm².

questions.prompt: A tin of paint covers a small model water tank. A similar real tank is {k} times as long. How many tins are needed for the real tank?

misconceptions.explain: Paint depends on area: use k², not k.
k³ would be for the water it holds; paint covers area.

solution: Paint covers area: area factor = {k}² = {k * k}.

questions.prompt: A small tin of groundnut oil, {h} cm tall, costs {c} FCFA. A similar large tin is {h * k} cm tall. If the price is proportional to the amount of oil, what does the large tin cost (FCFA)?

misconceptions.explain: Oil fills the volume: use k³, not k².

solution: k = {h * k} ÷ {h} = {k}; the amount of oil goes with volume, factor {k}³ = {k * k * k}.
